messages.content: You are a senior MongoDB data modeler migrating a relational app. Follow the guidebook rules exactly. Answer with ONE JSON object and nothing else.

GUIDEBOOK:
# Schema-design guidebook (input to the schema agent)

GOLDEN RULE: data that is accessed together is stored together, unless that would break a rule below.

R1 Embed vs reference. Embed child data when it is (a) read with the parent on hot endpoints, (b) bounded in count,
   and (c) rarely updated independently. Otherwise reference it (keep it in its own collection, keyed by the parent id).
R2 Bounded arrays only. An embedded array needs a known small upper bound (`maxItems`). Rows created by user
   activity (one row per user per parent: likes, follows, comments) are UNBOUNDED. Never embed them as arrays.
   Store them as their own collection, and keep a denormalized COUNTER on the parent if the count is read often.
R3 Many-to-many. Junction tables become either (a) a bounded array of keys/values on one side (e.g. a small tag
   list), or (b) a junction collection with a compound `_id` {a, b}, which makes writes idempotent, plus an index
   on the reverse direction.
R4 Self-references. Never embed a document of the same collection inside itself (it recurses without end). Model
   user→user relations as a junction collection.
R5 Extended reference. When a hot read shows a few fields of a parent (e.g. author name and avatar), you MAY copy
   those fields into the child ("extended reference"). Only do this when the copied fields change rarely, and every
   write to them updates the copies. Always also keep the parent id.
R6 Computed pattern / denormalized counters. Store counts that hot reads need (e.g. favorites count). The writes
   that change the underlying rows must also update the counter, in the same operation or transaction.
R7 16 MB limit. Estimated max document size must stay far below 16 MB (target < 1 MB).
R8 Recoverability. Every source table, row and column must remain recoverable from the target design (lossless).
R9 Identity. Use deterministic `_id`s derived from the source primary key (integers stay integers), so the
   migration is idempotent and every source row maps to exactly one document. Compound keys become `_id: {a, b}`.
R10 Indexes. Every query predicate and sort used by an endpoint needs a supporting index (equality fields first,
   then the sort field). Unique business keys get unique indexes.
R11 API contract. The HTTP responses must not change. Fields hidden by the old toJSON must stay hidden.


APPLICATION (Conduit, a Medium-like blog; Express + Sequelize + Postgres). Inventory produced by a static analyzer:
TABLES (column:type, PK, FKs, rows):
- Articles(id:int, slug:string, title:string, description:string, body:string, createdAt:date, updatedAt:date, userId:int) PK=['id'] FK=[userId->Users.id] rows=1000
- Comments(id:int, body:string, createdAt:date, updatedAt:date, articleId:int, userId:int) PK=['id'] FK=[userId->Users.id; articleId->Articles.id] rows=2038
- Favorites(articleId:int, userId:int) PK=['articleId', 'userId'] FK=[articleId->Articles.id; userId->Users.id] rows=841
- Followers(userId:int, followerId:int) PK=['userId', 'followerId'] FK=[followerId->Users.id; userId->Users.id] rows=654
- TagList(articleId:int, tagName:string) PK=['articleId', 'tagName'] FK=[tagName->Tags.name; articleId->Articles.id] rows=1957
- Tags(name:string) PK=['name'] FK=[] rows=20
- Users(id:int, email:string, username:string, bio:string, image:string, password:string, createdAt:date, updatedAt:date) PK=['id'] FK=[] rows=200
ASSOCIATIONS:
- Article belongsTo User as=author through=None [N:1]
- Article hasMany Comment as=None through=None [1:N]
- Article belongsToMany Tag as=tagList through=TagList [N:M]
- Article belongsToMany User as=None through=Favorites [N:M]
- Comment belongsTo Article as=None through=None [N:1]
- Comment belongsTo User as=author through=None [N:1]
- Tag belongsToMany Article as=None through=TagList [N:M]
- User hasMany Article as=None through=None [1:N]
- User hasMany Comment as=None through=None [1:N]
- User belongsToMany Article as=favorites through=Favorites [N:M]
- User belongsToMany User as=followers through=Followers [N:M self-referential]
- User belongsToMany User as=following through=Followers [N:M self-referential]
toJSON hides: Article:['id', 'userId']; Comment:['articleId', 'userId']; Tag:['id', 'userId', 'TagList']; User:['id', 'password', 'updatedAt', 'createdAt']
ACCESS PATTERNS (endpoint w=assumed weight: tables read together | written):
- GET /api/articles w=30: Articles,Favorites,Followers,TagList,Tags,Users | - (N+1 in original: 8 per-row queries)
- GET /api/articles/:slug w=25: Articles,Favorites,Followers,TagList,Tags,Users | -
- GET /api/articles/:slug/comments w=20: Articles,Comments,Followers,Users | - (N+1 in original: 5 per-row queries)
- GET /api/articles/feed w=15: Articles,Favorites,Followers,TagList,Tags,Users | - (N+1 in original: 8 per-row queries)
- GET /api/user w=10: Users | -
- GET /api/tags w=10: Tags | -
- GET /api/profiles/:username w=8: Followers,Users | -
- POST /api/users w=2: Users | Users
- POST /api/users/login w=2: Users | -
- PUT /api/user w=2: Users | Users
- POST /api/articles w=2: Articles,Favorites,Followers,Tags,Users | Articles,TagList,Tags,Users (N+1 in original: 4 per-row queries)
- PUT /api/articles/:slug w=2: Articles,Favorites,Followers,TagList,Tags,Users | Articles
- DELETE /api/articles/:slug w=2: Articles,TagList,Tags,Users | Articles
- POST /api/profiles/:username/follow w=2: Followers,Users | Followers
- DELETE /api/profiles/:username/follow w=2: Followers,Users | Followers
- POST /api/articles/:slug/favorite w=2: Articles,Favorites,Followers,TagList,Tags,Users | Favorites
- DELETE /api/articles/:slug/favorite w=2: Articles,Favorites,Followers,TagList,Tags,Users | Favorites
- POST /api/articles/:slug/comments w=2: Articles,Followers,Users | Comments
- DELETE /api/articles/:slug/comments/:commentId w=2: Comments,Users | Comments
QUERY PREDICATES (source level):
- Articles where [] sort createdAt desc
- Articles where ['slug']
- Articles where ['userId'] sort createdAt desc
- Comments where ['articleId']
- Favorites where ['articleId']
- Favorites where ['articleId', 'userId']
- Favorites where ['userId']
- Followers where ['followerId']
- Followers where ['followerId', 'userId']
- Followers where ['userId']
- TagList where ['articleId']
- TagList where ['tagName']
- Users where ['email']
- Users where ['username']

TASK: CONCEPTUAL schema design. For EVERY relationship/junction table decide embed vs reference, citing rule ids.
Return JSON:
{"relationships":[{"relationship":"...","cardinality":"...","decision":"embed array|extended reference|junction collection|reference|counter",
  "rules":["R1",...],"reason":"one sentence tied to an access pattern"}],
 "collections":[{"name":"...","source":"<table>","contains":"what is embedded/denormalized"}],
 "counters":[{"collection":"...","field":"...","counts":"<table>","maintainedBy":"which writes update it"}],
 "risks":["one line each"]}
